content.Beta-blockers: Beta-blockers are recommended in ACS patients with LVEF ≤40% regardless of HF symptoms. (Recommendation class I, level A)

RAAS system inhibitors.Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors: ACE inhibitors are recommended in ACS patients with HF symptoms, LVEF ≤40%, diabetes, hypertension, and/or CKD. (I, A)
RAAS system inhibitors.Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists: MR antagonists are recommended in ACS patients with LVEF ≤40% and HF or diabetes. (I, A)

content.Imaging: For patients with pre-discharge LVEF ≤40%, repeat evaluation of LVEF 6–12 weeks after an ACS (and after complete revascularization and institution of optimal medical therapy) is recommended to assess potential need for sudden cardiac death primary prevention ICD implantation. (I, C)
content.Vaccination: Influenza vaccination is recommended for all ACS patients. (I, A)
Recommendations for patient perspectives: Patient-centred care is recommended by assessing and adhering to individual patient preferences, needs and beliefs to ensure patient values inform clinical decisions. (I, B)

Include ACS patients in decision-making as much as condition allows; inform them about risks of adverse events, radiation exposure, and alternative options; use decision aids to facilitate discussion. (I, B)
Assess symptoms using methods that help patients describe their experience. (I, C)
content.Abbreviations noted on page: ACS = acute coronary syndrome; LVEF = left ventricular ejection fraction; HF = heart failure; CKD = chronic kidney disease; ICD = implantable cardioverter-defibrillator; ESC = European Society of Cardiology; hs-cTn = high-sensitivity cardiac troponin; other standard abbreviations listed.
